title: NHC rapid-intensification probabilities (2020-2025) were calibrated over water only in the SHIPS-RII consensus: its members had opposite errors and all SHIPS-RII models ignored land, unlike DTOPS
abstract: We verified the rapid-intensification (RI) probabilities in the public NHC ATCF e-decks for 2020-2025. The test included the SHIPS-RII discriminant (RIOD), logistic (RIOL) and Bayesian (RIOB) models, their consensus (RIOC), the ECMWF versions and DTOPS, at 8 thresholds. The truth was the final HURDAT2 best track. The plan was pre-registered. For 30 kt in 24 h there were 3,961 consensus forecasts (231 storms) and 277 RI events. The consensus was near calibrated: observed/expected 0.79 (95% storm bootstrap 0.58-1.00) in the Atlantic and 1.05 (0.82-1.28) in the eastern Pacific. This result came from opposite member errors: RIOD gave 1.5-2 times too many expected events (O/E 0.55 and 0.64) and RIOB gave 1.7-2.4 times too few (O/E 1.68 and 2.36). RIOB was over-confident (calibration slope 0.65-0.73) and gave at most 1% before 30% of all RI events. DTOPS was calibrated (0.97 and 1.15) and had the highest Brier skill (0.22 and 0.28). The main algorithmic source of the Atlantic over-forecast was land. When the issue-time consensus track crossed land within 24 h, the RIOC mean probability was 8.9% but RI occurred in 1.4% (O/E 0.16, 0.03-0.30); in the eastern Pacific there were 0 events against 5.3 expected. Over water, RIOC had O/E 0.99 and 1.09. The same land error occurred at all 8 thresholds. The RI models were developed only on over-water cases, and we found no land check in the operational code path that writes them. DTOPS takes intensity changes from land-aware models and lowered its probabilities over land. Initial-intensity differences between operational and best-track values were not a main source. In a 2023-2025 hold-out test, a land rule improved the Brier score of the consensus in all 16 threshold-basin cases (10 significant). A two-parameter recalibration did not help, because RI frequency changed between seasons. Limitations: six seasons only, endpoint best-track truth, and a straight-line consensus track for the land flag.

display.caption: Observed/expected RI counts (30 kt in 24 h, 2020-2025) for each technique. Filled markers: the issue-time TVCN track stays over water for 24 h. Open markers: the track crosses land. The SHIPS-RII members and their consensus over-forecast strongly when the track crosses land, but are near calibrated (consensus) over water. DTOPS lowers its probabilities over land. Bars are 95% storm-block bootstrap intervals; markers at the left edge mean zero observed events.

Reliability diagrams (30 kt in 24 h, all windows). The discriminant RIOD is below the diagonal (too high). The Bayesian RIOB is above the diagonal at low probabilities and below it at high probabilities, which shows over-confidence. The consensus RIOC and DTOPS are closest to the diagonal. Bins with fewer than 10 forecasts are not shown.

Mean forecast probability in land-crossing windows (solid lines) and in over-water windows (dotted lines) for the consensus RIOC and DTOPS, compared with the observed RI rate in land-crossing windows (crosses), at all 8 RI thresholds. The RIOC probabilities over land are equal to or higher than over water, and are 3-10 times the observed rate.
